parsedVerdict.reasoning: EnrolmentsService sits in the application layer and does application work. It runs the enrol and withdraw use cases, loads and saves records through injected repositories, and leaves the business decisions to the domain: course.admit() and enrolment.withinCoolingOff(). The rubric's fail conditions for an application file are web or transport artifacts: a request, response, HTTP context, status code or HTTP error in a signature or thrown. None of these appear here. The methods take string parameters and return Promise<Enrolment> or Promise<boolean>. The only error thrown is DomainError, which the project declares in its domain layer. The bans on framework decorators, ORM types and direct I/O apply only to domain files. So @Injectable, @InjectRepository and the TypeORM Repository<...> constructor parameters are allowed in an application service. They are dependency wiring for persistence entities from the infrastructure layer, which the application layer may depend on. The cohesion/broad-responsibility flag concerns how many responsibilities the class has, not whether its layer role is right. The source shows no misplaced layer responsibility, so the flag does not count against this rule.
